exercises.heading: 8.2. Exercises
exercises.instruction: 1, 2, 3, and 4 The given curve is rotated about the $$x$$ -axis. Set up, but do not evaluate, an integral for the area of the resulting surface by integrating with respect to $$x$$ and with respect to $$y$$ .

5, 6, 7, and 8 The given curve is rotated about the $$y$$ -axis. Set up, but do not evaluate, an integral for the area of the resulting surface by integrating with respect to $$x$$ and with respect to $$y$$ .
9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, and 16 Find the exact area of the surface obtained by rotating the curve about the $$x$$ -axis.
17, 18, 19, and 20 The given curve is rotated about the $$y$$ -axis. Find the area of the resulting surface.

21, 22, 23, 24, 25, and 26 Set up an integral for the area of the surface obtained by rotating the given curve about the specified axis. Then evaluate your integral numerically, correct to four decimal places.
27–28 Find the exact area of the surface obtained by rotating the given curve about the $$x$$ -axis.

29–30 Use a computer to find the exact area of the surface obtained by rotating the given curve about the $$y$$ -axis. If your software has trouble evaluating the integral, express the surface area as an integral in the other variable.

31–32 Use Simpson’s Rule with $$n = 10$$ to approximate the area of the surface obtained by rotating the given curve about the $$x$$ -axis. Compare your answer with the value of the integral produced by a calculator or computer.

problem.paragraph: Gabriel’s Horn The surface formed by rotating the curve $$y = 1/x$$ , $$x \geqslant 1$$ , about the $$x$$ -axis is known as Gabriel’s horn. Show that the surface area is infinite (although the enclosed volume is finite; see Exercise 7.8.75).

image.alt: Details The three dimensional rendering of a solid, and a curve are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The solid resembles a pipe with one end broader than the other, with the broad end facing the y axis. The sides slowly taper from the broad end to the narrow one, bulging slightly inward. The bulge is more on near the broader end and becomes gradually lesser as we proceed to the narrow end. The broad end is a circular region with its center at (1, 0). The curved profile of the top side is highlighted, tracing a curve labeled y = 1/x. The curve begins directly above (1, 0), goes down to the right, concave up, more and more gradually as we proceed to the right and ends at the topmost point of the narrow side of the solid.

problem.paragraph: If the infinite curve $$y = e^{- x}$$ , $$x \geqslant 0$$ , is rotated about the $$x$$ -axis, find the area of the resulting surface.

list.item: If $$a > 0$$ , find the area of the surface generated by rotating the loop of the curve $$3ay^{2} = x{({a - x})}^{2}$$ about the $$x$$ -axis.

Find the surface area if the loop is rotated about the $$y$$ -axis. Details A curve is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis has a single tick mark labeled a. The curve, labeled 3ay^2 = x*(a minus x)^2, enters from the top right corner, goes down the to left, concave up, crosses the x axis at a, traces a loop by descending below the x axis, then going up to the left, touching the y axis at the origin, going up to the right, concave down, then going down to the right, and crossing the x axis at a again, then goes down to the right, mimicking its entry and exits at the bottom right.

problem.paragraph: A group of engineers are building a parabolic satellite dish whose shape will be formed by rotating the curve $$y = ax^{2}$$ about the $$y$$ -axis. If the dish is to have a $$10$$ -ft diameter and a maximum depth of $$2$$ ft, find the value of $$a$$ and the surface area of the dish.

image.alt: A photograph of a satellite dish

list.item: The ellipse $${\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} + \frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1} a > b$$ is rotated about the $$x$$ -axis to form a surface called an ellipsoid, or prolate spheroid. Find the surface area of this ellipsoid.
If the ellipse in part (a) is rotated about its minor axis (the $$y$$ -axis), the resulting ellipsoid is called an oblate spheroid. Find the surface area of this ellipsoid.

problem.paragraph: Find the surface area of the torus in Exercise 6.2.75.

list.item: If the curve $$y = f(x)$$ , $$a \leqslant x \leqslant b$$ , is rotated about the horizontal line $$y = c$$ , where $$f(x) \leqslant c$$ , find a formula for the area of the resulting surface.

Set up an integral to find the area of the surface generated by rotating the curve $$y = \sqrt{x}$$ , $$0 \leqslant x \leqslant 4$$ , about the line $$y = 4$$ . Then evaluate the integral numerically, correct to four decimal places.

problem.paragraph: Set up an integral for the area of the surface obtained by rotating the curve $$y = x^{3}$$ , $$1 \leqslant x \leqslant 2$$ , about the given line. Then evaluate the integral numerically, correct to two decimal places.
Find the area of the surface obtained by rotating the circle $$x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}$$ about the line $$y = r$$ .

exercises.instruction: 42–43 Zone of a Sphere A zone of a sphere is the portion of the sphere that lies between two parallel planes.

problem.paragraph: Show that the surface area of a zone of a sphere is $$S = 2\pi Rh$$ , where $$R$$ is the radius of the sphere and $$h$$ is the distance between the planes. (Notice that $$S$$ depends only on the distance between the planes and not on their location, provided that both planes intersect the sphere.)
Show that the surface area of a zone of a cylinder with radius $$R$$ and height $$h$$ is the same as the surface area of the zone of a sphere in Exercise 42.

Let $$L$$ be the length of the curve $$y = f(x)$$ , $$a \leqslant x \leqslant b$$ , where $$f$$ is positive and has a continuous derivative. Let $$S_{f}$$ be the surface area generated by rotating the curve about the $$x$$ -axis. If $$c$$ is a positive constant, define $$g(x) = f(x) + c$$ and let $$S_{g}$$ be the corresponding surface area generated by the curve $$y = g(x)$$ , $$a \leqslant x \leqslant b$$ . Express $$S_{g}$$ in terms of $$S_{f}$$ and $$L$$ .

Show that if we rotate the curve $$y = e^{ x/2} + e^{- x/2}$$ about the $$x$$ -axis, the area of the resulting surface is the same value as the enclosed volume for any interval $$a \leqslant x \leqslant b$$ .
